description: IBCS vertical variance waterfall (EX 1.1 card 29): reference total (PY/PL) at the top from the axis, the variance by structure element as floating bars (impact colour, signed labels outside), the primary total (AC/FC) at the bottom, assisting lines, and the total variance arrow under the result. Options: scale band (CH 4.3) and a highlighting ellipse on one value (UN 5.1).

fields.Category: text, row label; sort the visual in the intended element/report order (blank labels are dropped)
fields.Kind: optional text: base | variance (or element) | total. Omit for element-only input with BaseValue/TotalValue; omitted/blank Kind means variance
fields.Value: measure: base = reference value; variance/element = SIGNED CONTRIBUTION to the total; total = primary value. For a cost line in a margin bridge bind −ΔCOS with Polarity +1, not raw ΔCOS
fields.Polarity: optional measure 1 / -1 / 0; else the polarity knob
fields.PxPerUnit: optional measure, same value on every row: px per display unit for the page's scale group; wins over pxPerUnit
fields.BaseValue: optional measure on element rows: starting/reference value; the first non-null value in visual row order synthesizes a base bar unless an explicit Kind base row exists. Values are before unitDivisor
fields.TotalValue: optional measure on element rows: primary/result value; the first non-null value in visual row order synthesizes a total bar unless an explicit Kind total row exists. Values are before unitDivisor
fields.ScaleBand: optional measure, same value on every row: scale band value in data units (before unitDivisor); wins over scaleBand
fields.Highlight: optional measure: 1 on the row whose value label gets the highlighting ellipse (the value the key message cites); blank or 0 = none

ibcs.notes: Value is the contribution to the total, not necessarily the source measure delta: for a cost line in a margin bridge bind −ΔCOS with Polarity +1. A cost increase therefore contributes a negative step (unfavourable), and a cost reduction contributes a positive step (favourable). Polarity changes only impact colour; geometry always follows the contribution sign. Include a remainder row (e.g. Rest) so base + Σ contribution = total. If they do not reconcile, the arrow label shows the difference with a '!'. Two waterfalls of one unit: the same pxPerUnit and labelWidth, and each visual's width sized to its own range (usermeta.ibcs.layout). Rounded-zero rule: abs(value) × 10^decimals < 0.5 is labelled 0 without sign and gets no impact colour. Input formats: (1) explicit Kind rows, with base/total values in Value; (2) one model row per element, Value as the signed contribution, optional Kind omitted, and BaseValue/TotalValue measures repeated on element rows. The template uses the first non-null value of each anchor independently in visual row order, creates each missing anchor once, and keeps explicit base/total rows when present. baseLabel/totalLabel name only the synthesized bars. Repeated anchor measures must be constant in the current filter context. Blank categories and rows whose Value, BaseValue and TotalValue are all null are dropped; zero is a value, and an anchor-only row is retained. PxPerUnit alone do not retain an unknown N/A member. Scale band (CH 4.3): set scaleBand (or bind ScaleBand) to the same round value in every chart of the unit whose scales differ (e.g. a waterfall by month next to one by entity at another px per unit). Highlight (UN 5.1): knob highlight = the row label, or field Highlight = 1 on that row, draws the blue ellipse around its value label; one highlighted value per chart, the one the key message names. With pxPerUnit = 0 the scale leaves room for the widest label (measured like bar-structure-variance) beyond the 34 px right padding, so labels are never cut at the visual edge. Short bars (small values under a fixed pxPerUnit): a base or total label that does not fit inside its bar sits right of the bar in the text colour, and a negative variance label that would come closer than valueLabelGap px to the category axis moves to the far (right) end of its bar, so value labels never run into the category labels. Scenario names: the base and total bars are named once. When their row label (Category) already contains the scenario code (refScenario / minuend as a word, e.g. 'PY', 'AC 2026'), the extra legend text at the bar is left out; with neutral labels ('Start', 'Result') it is drawn.

layout.plusCategoryLabels: width of the longest row label in px + 6 (Vega measures the text; about 7 px per character at 12 px Segoe UI); labelWidth does not reserve it
layout.rule: container width = fixedPx + row labels + (hi − lo) × pxPerUnit + padHigh; measured with Vega-Lite 6.4.3 at ibcsFontSize 12; a highlighting ellipse reaches 5 px beyond its label on each side: keep ibcsLabelPx (right pad) large enough when the highlighted label is the rightmost one; the other dimension (height) = rows × the row step + crossFixedPx (50: padding top 16 for the scale-band label and bottom 34 for the total-variance marker and its label), which scale_layout.py adds when categoryCount is given

previewVariants.note: Element-only input: independent first non-null anchors, repeated measures, zero/rounded-zero steps, anchor-only row, blank/unknown category filtering. Later anchor values deliberately differ to verify that the first non-null value wins.
Margin bridge: Standard cost is −ΔCOS with Polarity +1, so a cost increase moves left and is unfavourable; a cost reduction moves right and is favourable.
A negative step whose label would sit on the vertical assisting line from the base end: the label moves left of that line.
Scale band at 5 display units and the highlighting ellipse on one variance label.

Short bars under a fixed pxPerUnit: base and total labels that do not fit inside their bar sit right of it, and a negative variance label that would reach the category labels moves to the far end of its bar.

params.name: baseLabel
params.description: row label of the synthesized BaseValue bar; explicit Kind base rows keep their own label

params.name: totalLabel
params.description: row label of the synthesized TotalValue bar; explicit Kind total rows keep their own label

params.name: refScenario
params.description: name and notation of the base bar: 'PY' (solid light) or a plan code such as 'PL' or 'BU' (outlined)

params.name: minuend
params.description: name and notation of the total bar: 'AC' (solid) or 'FC' (hatched)

params.name: polarity
params.description: 1 higher is better, -1 lower is better, 0 neutral (blue): impact colour only, never the direction (a Polarity field per row wins where the template reads one)

params.name: decimals
params.description: decimals of every value label (display units); also the precision of the rounded-zero rule

params.name: unitDivisor
params.description: divides every value before drawing and labelling: 1 = the measures are already scaled (preferred, e.g. a scaled measure or a Scale picker), 1000 = thousands, 1000000 = millions. The unit belongs in the title (UN 2.2), never as K/M suffixes

params.name: xMax
params.description: right end of the value scale in display units; 0 = from the data. A shared DOMAIN: same xMax gives the same px per unit only on waterfalls of the same width and labelWidth. For a same-unit scale group use pxPerUnit instead

params.name: pxPerUnit
params.description: px per display unit (after unitDivisor) on the value axis; 0 = off. When set, the domain is the plot width ÷ pxPerUnit, anchored at the left end (zero), so two waterfalls of one unit show the same px per unit. Size the container to the data (usermeta.ibcs.layout, scripts/scale_layout.py of the ibcs-power-bi skill). If the container is too small, the data wins and the px per unit shrinks: nothing is cut

params.name: ibcsLabelPx
params.description: label room in px right of the longest bar (pxPerUnit > 0 only)

params.name: ibcsCharWidth
params.description: estimated width of one label character as a share of ibcsFontSize; with pxPerUnit = 0 the value scale leaves room inside the plot for the widest label beyond the 34 px right padding, so labels are never cut at the visual edge

params.name: valueLabelGap
params.description: minimum px between a value label and the category axis: a negative variance label that would come closer (short bars, a small base under a fixed pxPerUnit) is drawn right of its bar instead, so it never runs into the category labels

params.name: labelWidth
params.description: px reserved for the row labels when the container is narrow; the label column is measured from the text, pass its width to scale_layout.py

params.name: scaleBand
params.description: scale band (CH 4.3) in display units: a light area from the axis to this value and a labelled line, the same round value in every chart of the unit whose scales differ; 0 = off (field ScaleBand wins, in data units before unitDivisor)

params.name: highlight
params.description: row label (Category, or baseLabel / totalLabel for the synthesized bars) whose value label gets the blue highlighting ellipse (UN 5.1): the value the key message cites; '' = none. The field Highlight (1 on the row) does the same from the model

params.name: stepScale
params.description: multiplies the category step (ibcsCategoryStep), keep it identical for every chart of the page

(highlight != '' && (datum._copy == 1 ? baseLabel : datum._copy == 2 ? totalLabel : datum['Category']) == highlight) || (datum._copy == 0 && isValid(datum['Highlight']) && datum['Highlight'] !== '' && datum['Highlight'] !== 0 && datum['Highlight'] !== false)
datum._copy == 1 ? datum['BaseValue'] / unitDivisor : datum._copy == 2 ? datum['TotalValue'] / unitDivisor : isValid(datum['Value']) ? datum['Value'] / unitDivisor : null
!isValid(datum._val) || abs(datum._val) * pow(10, decimals) < 0.5 ? null : datum._pol == 0 ? ibcsNeutral : (datum._val * datum._pol > 0 ? ibcsGood : ibcsBad)
!isValid(datum._val) ? 'N/A' : (datum._k == 'variance' ? (abs(datum._val) * pow(10, decimals) < 0.5 ? format(0, datum._fa) : format(datum._val, datum._fv)) : format(datum._val, datum._fa))
datum._ppu > 0 ? max(datum._xmax + max(ibcsLabelPx, datum._room) / datum._ppu, width / datum._ppu) : datum._xmax + datum._room * datum._xmax / max(width - datum._room, 1)
!isValid(datum._delta) || abs(datum._delta) * pow(10, decimals) < 0.5 ? null : datum._pol == 0 ? ibcsNeutral : (datum._delta * datum._pol > 0 ? ibcsGood : ibcsBad)
